display.title: King David's Grave and the King's Lost Sword
display.summary_short: A visiting king drops his precious sword into the sealed cave of King David's tomb. Only a rabbi, after the whole community says Tehillim, can bring it back.
display.summary_long: Told in honor of Dovid HaMelech, whose yahrzeit is on Shavuos. A king visits Yerushalayim and asks to see the burial place of King David, but finds it sealed off: everyone who went down into the cave never came back alive. He lowers a candle through the iron bars to peek inside, and his royal sword, a family heirloom with a large diamond on its handle, slips into the cave. The king orders the bars removed and sends down two servants on ropes, and neither returns. Then he has an idea: King David was a Jew, so he will surely protect a Jew. He calls for the head rabbi, who asks for no reward, only time to gather the community. The Jews say the entire Tehillim, the book King David wrote, and the rabbi is lowered into the cave. To everyone's joy he comes up with the sword. He tells the king to thank Hashem, not him, and the king grants the Jews of his land full freedom to keep the Torah. Asked what he saw, the rabbi says only a very bright light: Dovid Melech Yisroel chai v'kayam, King David is truly alive.
display.lesson: Hashem protects those who turn to Him in prayer, and thanks belong to Hashem; Dovid HaMelech lives on.
